title: Clear the lint blocking a Galaxy S24's charging port with a soft toothbrush, without packing it deeper, and wipe it off
keywords: depth control in a 2.56 mm slot
do not pack the debris deeper
instruction: Brush the lint out of the phone's charging port with the toothbrush, wipe the lint off onto the paper towel, then lay the toothbrush down.
context: Samsung's support pages: "Dust or foreign material inside the charging port is one of the most common causes of charging issues", and "Remove debris using a soft brush", without metal objects. Loose pocket lint that has just collected beside the port's tongue brushes out; pushed to the back wall (by a jab or by the plug) it packs, assumed here to no longer brush out. The bristles must reach it 4.5 mm down a 2.56 mm slot, hook it out with a sideways stroke and stop short of the back.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Samsung Galaxy S24 SM-S921B phone (147.0 x 70.6 x 7.6, 167 g), switched off, standing upside down in an aluminium desk phone stand so its USB-C port is on top: screen toward the arms, leaning back 12 degrees from vertical, its lower (real top) edge centred at x 300, y -40, 7 up; the port's mouth centred at x 331, y -40, 151 up, its 8.34 long side along y. Port: opening 8.34 x 2.56, tongue 6.69 x 0.70 (USB Type-C); depth 7.5 and the tongue's top 2.0 below the mouth are estimates. Stand: 76 x 76 x 3 base centred at x 318, y -40, a ledge with an 8 high front lip under the phone, an 85 long back rest at the same lean, about 120 g, on a non-slip pad. Lint: four 2 mm balls of grey dryer lint (cotton/polyester), one wedged in each of the two 0.93 gaps beside the tongue at 2.2 either side of the port's centre, 4.5 below the mouth (reset notes). Toothbrush: Oral-B Indicator Contour Clean 35 Soft (about 190 long, handle 13 wide x 9 thick, head 28 x 11, bristle field 25 x 10, bristles 11 tall, 16 g; estimates), lying bristles-down with its handle along y and its head toward the phone; the point on the handle 85 mm from the head's centre is at x 220, y -220 (lot A, screenshot) or x 255, y -265 (lot B). Paper towel: one Bounty sheet folded in quarters, about 140 x 130, flat, centred at x 420, y -200. Trials run lots A and B and are averaged. Real trial: the phone stays switched off and only its body and port are used, so any used Galaxy S24 in any cosmetic grade will do (refurbished from about US$220 at Back Market, against US$799.99 new); with the stand, toothbrush, towel and a 0.5 mm rule the parts cost about US$250-350 (README).
scoring: Read from the overhead and side close-up videos (30 fps), flashlight macro photos of the port square-on with a 0.5 mm rule, and a photo of the towel. Score 0 for the trial if at any moment: the bristles go over 6.5 mm into the port (a pen line round them 6.5 mm from the tips passes below the mouth); a robot finger or the brush's head or handle touches the phone's top edge; the phone moves over 6 mm or tips over 4 degrees in its stand (side video); the phone or the toothbrush falls off the counter. Every score needs, for the last 1 s, the toothbrush let go on the counter or towel at least 5 mm from the phone and stand, both hands at least 30 mm from the phone and brush, and both still. A tuft is left in the port if any lint fibre 0.5 mm or longer remains in its quarter of the opening. 1.0: none left and all 4 tufts on the towel. 0.75: none left. 0.5: 1 or 2 left. 0.25: 3 left. 0 otherwise. Lots A and B averaged.
run_limit: 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: 1. Phone off and unplugged. Photograph the port square-on under a flashlight with a 0.5 mm rule in view. 2. Roll four 2 mm balls of grey cotton/polyester dryer lint (no glue). Push each with a 0.5 mm wire marked at 4.5 mm into its gap beside the tongue (left and right of it, near each end) until the mark meets the mouth; it wedges there. Redo one that sinks deeper than 5.5 mm. Photograph again. 3. Draw a pen line round the bristles 6.5 mm from their tips; use a clean, dry brush. 4. Lay a fresh folded towel and the brush at the lot's places. Lint and towel are consumed.
fidelity: True size: phone (Samsung's dimensions), USB-C opening and tongue (Type-C spec); port depth, brush and stand sizes are estimates; all boxes. The bristle field is a rigid box: it rests and wipes on the counter and towel but has no collision with the phone's top 14 mm. Lint is a stated rule, drawn: hooked once tips 4.0 mm deep or more beside it move 2 mm sideways; scraped off if dragged past the slot's end; on the towel after 10 mm of slide; tips past 6.5 mm pack it. No charging.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (A 0.0, B 0.0; both ran to the 1,800-step limit without refusing; the toothbrush was not picked up and no rule was broken). Demo: 1.0 in A and B (all four tufts out and wiped onto the towel, toothbrush laid down, released and still; about 28 s each).
